title: Sec huddle — deep dive: vuln triage, secrets, threat modeling
content:
Attendees: Aisha K (owner), Liam O, Sofia M, Marcus C, Hannah P, + quick drop-in from Eng oncall (Vik)

Duration: 45m (standup-style deep dive)
Location: Zoom / note capture

Purpose: sync on current vuln backlog, confirm secrets exposure triage, and align on a short threat-modeling spike for the Dedicated control-plane change next sprint.

Agenda:
- Quick backlog refresh (top 6 tickets)
- Secrets incidents: recent s3-cred exposure false-positive and follow-up plan
- Threat-modeling kickoff: Dedicated control-plane change (KMS rotation, cross-region fallbacks)
- Action item assignments and hotfix priorities

Notes / Discussion:
1) Backlog snapshot
- Top priorities reviewed (list filtered by exploitability + customer impact):
  - SEC-2179: token refresh endpoint unauthenticated redirect chain — severity: high; risk: session hijack if misrouted. Repro steps in ticket. Ownership: Marcus. ETA: patch + tests by 2026-12-22.
  - SEC-2140: dependency libheap v2.3 (transitive) -> known RCE POI. We're on v2.1. Mitigation: upgrade to v2.4 or apply sandboxing. Engineering estimated 3d for upgrade across infra images. Owner: Sofia.
  - SEC-2201: telemetry aggregator leaking partial user ids in logs (low probability, high sensitivity). Quick fix: scrub before write + audit 48h logs. Owner: Liam.
  - INFRA-6420: kube admission webhook misconfig limiting namespace RBAC — causing elevated pod privileges in staging (medium). Owner: Hannah (infra). Target: 2026-12-24.
  - SEC-2210: secrets-scan false-positive (aws key) flagged by our scanner last night. Investigated below.

2) Secrets triage — false positive vs real exposure
- Incident: nightly scanner flagged an AWS access key in commit history (repo: platform/ops-scripts). Scanner attached full line and file path; on first glance looked legit.
- Quick investigation: key truncated and annotated (example token: AKIAxxxx—EXPIRED). Confirmed key is rotated and marked as revoked in IAM (timestamp 2026-11-12). Commit msg showed it was intentionally left as redaction placeholder for docs.
- Root cause: our secrets scanner rule is too permissive for well-formed truncated placeholders and doc stubs. Causes noisy oncall alerts.
- Decision: relax rule to require full-length matching pattern OR check commit age + IAM lookup for active keys before paging oncall. Temporary suppression for repo platform/docs until rule update.
- Actions:
  - Aisha: file follow-up SEC-2213 (scanner rule tuning) — due 2026-12-23.
  - Marcus: add quick IAM API check in the scanner playbook to mark revoked keys as low priority — due 2026-12-22.
  - Note to self: keep suppression windows short. Avoid blanket repo suppressions.

3) Threat modeling kickoff — Dedicated control-plane change
- Context: Product is proposing a change to Dedicated control-plane to allow customer-specific KMS keys with optional cross-region key fallback. This impacts key management, audit, and routing.
- Goals for spike (1 week):
  - enumerate attacker surfaces introduced by KMS cross-region fallback
  - define key rotation and compromise scenarios
  - propose mitigation patterns (fail-closed vs fail-open, policy enforcement points)
- Preliminary threats surfaced:
  - Threat A: lateral movement from compromised admin account in one region to customer key in fallback region (privilege escalation). Mitigation: strict cross-account roles, limited machine identities.
  - Threat B: replication lag causes stale access policies to be used; attacker windows open during rollback. Mitigation: version-check on key policy retrieval, short TTLs, monotonic policy revisions.
  - Threat C: telemetry leakage: KMS key IDs in logs exposing mapping between customer and region. Mitigation: redaction, hash mapping in observability layer.
- Assigned:
  - Hannah + Marcus: run a mini blast-radius matrix and identify 3 worst-case scenarios (deliverable: matrix doc) — due 2026-12-27.
  - Sofia: draft proposed policy enforcement diagram and PR for control-plane (start 2026-12-21). Include recommended IAM role scoping and least privilege templates.
  - Aisha: consolidate and run 30-min design review with product next Wed (2026-12-30).

4) Oncall and incident playbooks
- Observed pain: oncall ran into friction when scanner pages include raw stack traces with possible PII. Need to sanitize alerts.
- Action items:
  - Quick change: add default stack trace scrubber to alert payloads (Marcus) — 2026-12-22.
  - Medium: update oncall runbook to include steps for "secrets false positive" triage (Aisha + Liam) — 2026-12-28.

5) Quick wins / immediate hotfixes
- Marcus to push minimal validation on token-refresh redirect (SEC-2179) and create test that asserts redirect targets map to whitelisted domains. (hotfix branch created: gh/pr/1893)
- Sofia to open dependency bump MR for libheap and schedule rollout in canary first (INFRA-6420 capture in infra sprint). If upgrade causes perf regression, fallback plan is to containerize that component and apply seccomp.

6) Open questions / unresolved
- Should we automate IAM lookup during secrets scans (pros: fewer pages; cons: increased scan time and rate-limit on AWS APIs)? Team leaning: yes, but add caching and parallelism limits.
- For Dedicated KMS model: do we allow customer-managed CMKs in-host (bring-your-own-key) or require keys to be external KMS only? Product leaning external KMS for auditability, but P0 customers request BYOK. Need risk matrix.
- Do we introduce a blanket policy to redact KMS key IDs in all logs? Practical impact on debugging to be explored.

Logistics / follow-ups
- Weekly huddle cadence: keep Tuesday deep-dive; set 30-min Thursday quick triage for immediate escalations.
- Next deep-dive: 2026-12-27 — focus on SEC-2179 remediation verification, scanner rule changes, and KMS threat matrix first draft.

Decisions recorded (short):
- Suppress noisy scanner alerts for repo platform/docs while rule tuned (temporary). Owner: Aisha.
- Add IAM active-key check to scanner so revoked keys are deprioritized. Owner: Marcus.
- Begin 1-week threat modeling spike for Dedicated control-plane KMS changes. Owners: Hannah / Marcus / Sofia.

Appendix / handy links referenced during call:
- JIRA: SEC-2179 (token redirect)
- JIRA: SEC-2213 (scanner rule tuning) — placeholder
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1893
- Infra ticket: INFRA-6420
- Slack thread: #sec-ops (Dec 19) — sequence of screenshots from nightly scan

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep triage lightweight; aim to remove false positives from paging ASAP — oncall burn is real over holiday period.
- When writing playbook steps, include clear "why" for each action; people skip steps if they don't understand risk model.
- Double-check any suppression windows with product before applying to repos tied to compliance docs.

Status: draft notes — will iterate after Marcus uploads patch and scanner rule PR.
